acceptedAnswer.text: Influencer marketing is the work of partnering with creators whose audience matches your buyers, so their content introduces and recommends your product.

mainEntity.name: How does influencer marketing work with MMC?

acceptedAnswer.text: We shortlist for audience fit, brief against one idea, help agree deliverables and usage rights, track results to sales and reuse the best content as ads. Creators disclose paid partnerships as advertising rules require.

A monthly scope, agreed after a call. It is written down so you can see what each month covers. We do not publish a price list, because the right scope depends on your site, your market and how much you want done.
No. We cannot guarantee reach or sales from any creator. We commit to choosing for fit, clear terms, tracking and honest reporting.
D2C brands that sell products a creator can show. It also applies to B2B and education brands: the same method, measured on qualified leads, enquiries and admissions instead of orders.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your product, brand guidelines, a budget range for creators, tracking set up on your store, and a person who can approve briefs.

points.title: Fit over reach
points.text: Creators chosen for who follows them, not how many.

points.text: Terms that allow the best content to run as ads.

leaks.note: Screens are illustrative recreations of each platform's interface, not client data. Platform names and logos belong to their owners.
leaks.lede: Creators can introduce a brand well or waste a budget. Each stage below is where it goes wrong, and how we run it.

stages.why: A large audience that does not match your buyer produces reach, not sales.
stages.does: We shortlist creators by audience fit, engagement quality and past content, and check them before you commit.

stages.breaks: Sending a product and hoping for the best.
stages.why: Creators know their audience, but need to know the one thing you want said, and what to avoid.
stages.does: We write clear briefs around a single brand idea, leaving room for the creator's own voice.

stages.breaks: Paying for a post with no rights to reuse it.
stages.why: If you cannot run the content as an ad, you lose its best use.
stages.does: We agree deliverables, timelines and usage rights up front, including the right to run the content as ads.

stages.breaks: Judging campaigns on views and likes.
stages.why: Views do not show whether anyone bought. Links, codes and blended sales do.
stages.does: We give each creator tracked links and codes and read results alongside your total sales.

stages.breaks: Letting a great post disappear after a day.
stages.why: A post that earned attention organically often works as an ad too.
stages.does: We take the best creator content, with agreed rights, and run it as paid ads.

good.t: You sell a product a creator can show, and you can track sales.
good.why: D2C brands get creator content that doubles as ad creative, and consumer-facing education and B2B brands can use it for trust.

not.t: You want reach with no tracking, or one big name to fix everything.
not.why: Fit and tracking decide results, and a big name rarely substitutes for either.
